--no_truncate.help: Display all the chunk contents (Ignore the `max-visualize-chunk-size` configuration).

--off.help: Do not show the section(s) in subsequent context commands even though they might be in the 'context-sections' list.

--offset.help: Do a lookup instead of printing the sequence (accepts constant values as well as expressions)

--on.help: Show the section(s) in subsequent context commands again. The section(s) have to be in the 'context-sections' list.

--only-funcptrs.help: Spray only addresses whose values points to executable pages

--order.help: Displays/searches lists only with the specified order.

--page_name.help: Substring required to be part of the name of any found pages

--partial-overwrite.help: Consider partial overwrite candidates, default behavior only shows word-size overwrites.

--point-to.help: Mapping name of the page that you want the pointers point to

--pthread-self.help: Try to get the address of TLS by calling pthread_self().

--quiet.help: Do not output any message on success

--range.help: dash separated range of MSRs to read (eg. --range=1-10 where 10 is included)

--refresh.help: Drop the cached memory map (used by default on macOS) and re-fetch it. See the `vmmap-cache` config option.

--relative-addresses.help: Use offsets instead of absolute addresses in the report.

--retry.help: retry until a target is found

--reverse.help: Number of lines to show before the address.

--save-as.help: Sets the filename for the output of this command [e.g. --save-as='out.txt']

--sentinel.help: The address that stands in for an end of list marker in a non-cyclic list

--set.help: sets the kernel task used for supported pwndbg commands (kfile, kstack, knamespace, ksighand, kseccomp, pagewalk, vmmap), this option does not change internal memory (only effects how certain commands behaves)

--shallow.help: Return the biggest slot which contains this address, don't recurse for smaller slots. The group  which owns this slot will not be a nested group.

--show.help: Show the source code of an existing custom structure

--show-all.help: Force displaying of all theme options.

--show-readonly.help: Also display read-only entries (which are filtered out by default).

--so-name.help: Selects objects whose names matche the given expression

--step.help: Step to add between pointers so they are considered. For example, if this is 4 it would only consider pointers at an offset divisible by 4 from the starting pointer

--symbols.help: Show symbols for/of gadgets (if there are any)

--total.help: Total number of lines to show. This results in dynamic number of forward instructions depending on how many cached instructions are used.

--trunc-out.help: Truncate the output to 20 results. Differs from --limit in that it will first save all search results

--user.help: username or uid to filter by

--value.help: Value to spray memory with, when prefixed with '0x' treated as hex string encoded big-endian

--wait-for.help: Tells the debugger to wait for a process with the given pid or name to launch before attaching.

--where.help: Annotate each allocation/free with the calling symbol.

--writable.help: Only show functions whose GOT entry is in a writable region of memory

--zero.help: Encode the shellcode to avoid NULL bytes

--zone.help: Displays/searches lists only in the specified zone.

-n.help: Minimum length of ASCII strings to include

add.help: Add a custom structure and load it into the debugger

addr_end.help: Optional inclusive upper bound for chunk start addresses.

addr_start.help: Address of the first chunk (malloc_chunk struct start, prev_size field).

address.help: The address to get the enhanced instruction from - must be in cache.

address_or_module.help: Address or module name to dump

args.help: The arguments to run the binary with.

banner.help: Where a banner should be placed: both, top , bottom, none

binary_addr.help: Memory address of the decompiled binary in the address space

binary_path.help: File path of the decompiled binary as loaded in memory

binja.help: Install the Binary Ninja decompiler plugin

branch.help: The branch instruction to break on.

clearing.help: Indicates whether to clear the output

cmd.help:
Command to be used with the expression.
- eval: the expression is parsed and evaluated as in the debugged language.
- execute: the expression is executed as a GDB command.

comment.help: The text you want to comment

config_name.help: A config name to search for

contains.help: Get the cache for an address.

count.help: The number of entries to go forward in history

cpsr_value.help: Parse the given CPSR value instead of the actual one.

dump.help: Dump all nftables: tables, chains, rules, expressions

edit.help: Edit a custom structure and reload it

emulate.help: Whether to emulate instructions to find the next ones or just linearly disassemble.

err.help: Errno; if not passed, it is retrieved from __errno_location

explain.help: Gives a quick explanation of musl's mallocng allocator.

expression.help: The expression to be evaluated and shown in context

extent-info.help: Prints extent information for the given address

fake.help: If the chunk is a fake chunk.

fd.help: File descriptor of the file to be mapped, or -1 if using MAP_ANONYMOUS.

fdnum.help: File descriptor (FD) number to be replaced with the specified new socket or file.

filename.help: Name (path) of the file to save the cyclic pattern to

filter_.help: Only show caches that contain the given filter string

filter_pattern.help: Filter to apply to config parameters names/descriptions

find.help: Find slot which contains the given address.

find-extent.help: Returns extent information for pointer address allocated by jemalloc

flag.help: Flag for which you want to change the value

flags.help: Flags enum or int as in mmap(2). Eg. "MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS" or 0x22.

frame_type.help: The type of frame to print

func.help: Function to be decompiled. Defaults to the current function.

group.help: Print out information about a mallocng group at the given address.

height.help: Sets a fixed height (used for number of lines to display before cutoff). Only applies to sections where more data can be displayed like disasm, stack, and threads and overrides their section specific limits. Set to None for auto

hex_string.help: Hexadecimal string to convert (e.g., '00 70 75 c1 cd ef 59 00').

i.help: Index of the argument to print out.

info.help: Give an overview of the GOT tracker

jump.help: Make the decompiler's cursor jump to the PC

length.help: Length of the mapping, in bytes. Needs to be greater than zero.

lines.help: Number of lines of decompilation to show.

list.help: List the variables for the current stack frame

list-chains.help: Dump netfilter chains from a specific table

list-exprs.help: Dump only expressions from specific rule

list-flowtables.help: Dump netfilter flowtables from a specific table

list-objects.help: Dump netfilter objects from a specific table

list-rules.help: Dump netfilter rules from a specific chain

list-sets.help: Dump netfilter sets from a specific table

list-tables.help: Dump netfilter tables from a specific network namespace

load.help: Load a previously added structure into the debugger

max_candidate_size.help: Maximum size of fake chunks to find.

max_distance.help: Max acceptable distance between memory page boundry and leaked pointer

meta.help: Print out information about a mallocng group given the address of its meta.

metaarea.help: Print out a mallocng meta_area object at the given address.

module.help: Module to choose as base. Defaults to the target executable.

module_name.help: A module name substring to filter for

n.help: The number of stack frames to go down.

name.help: Name placed into output pstats filename

needle.help: The string to search for in the context history

newfile.help:
Specify a file or a socket.

For files, the filename must start with `/` (e.g., `/etc/passwd`).

For sockets, the following formats are allowed:
- `127.0.0.1:80` (default is TCP)
- `tcp://[::1]:80`
- `udp://example.com:80`
- `tcp+ipv6://example.com:80`

next.help: The name of the field pointing to the next element in the list

num.help: The expression number to be removed from context

num_threads.help: Number of threads to display. Omit to display all threads.

offset.help: Offset from the start of the file, in bytes, if using file based mapping.

page_names.help:
Mapping to search [e.g. libc].
Can be used with multiple mappings [e.g libc heap stack]

path.help: The path to which the output is written

prot.help: Prot enum or int as in mmap(2). Eg. "PROT_READ|PROT_EXEC" or 7 (for RWX).

query.help: Queries detailed tracking information about a single entry in the GOT

remove.help: Remove a custom structure and unload it from the debugger

section.help: The section to search in. If not provided, search in all sections

setbase.help: Manually set the base memory address of the decompiled binary

setpath.help: Manually set the path of the binary as loaded in memory

show-all.help: Show the names of all stored structures

size.help: Size of the address space, in bytes

slots.help: Dump information about a mallocng slot, given its start address.

slotu.help: Dump information about a mallocng slot, given its user address.

state.help: Turn ASLR on or off (takes effect when target is started)

symbol.help: Address or symbol name to lookup

symbol_regex.help: A regex matching the name of next symbol to be broken on before calling.

syscall.help: Syscall number (e.g., 1, 0x3c) or name (e.g., write, exit)

syscall_name.help: A syscall name to search for

table_family.help: Table family, eg: inet, ip, ip6, netdev, bridge, arp

target.help: pid, process name, part of cmdline to be matched or device file to attach to (uses current loaded file name if not provided)

target_address.help: Address of the word-sized value to overlap.

task_name.help: A task name to search for

toggle-break.help: Toggles whether possible UAF conditions will pause execution

ty.help: Go type of value to dump, e.g. map[int]string, or the address of a type to resolve at runtime, e.g. 0x408860

typename.help: The name of the structure being dumped. Use quotes if the type contains spaces (e.g. "struct malloc_state").

value.help: Value to which you want to set the flag - only valid options are 0 and 1

verbose.help: Whether to show more details or not.

which.help: Index of the breakpoint to clear.

width.help: Sets a fixed width (used for banner). Set to None for auto
